title: Electrospray Ionization Mass Spectrometry Insights into the Assembly of Lanthanide-Containing Clusters
claim: Changing a ligand's steric and coordination features can redirect the connection of lanthanide–titanium building blocks and yield a different cluster topology.
explanation: Replacing salicylic-acid-based motifs with 5-methoxysalicylic-acid-based motifs changed coordination pockets and peripheral-ligand orientation in the reported system, enabling chiral ring assemblies rather than the prior connection pattern.
scope: The reviewed lanthanide–titanium salicylate building-block systems.
conditions: Use of 5-methoxysalicylic acid and additional Ti(IV)-containing units in the described assembly.
caveats: The particular ring topology and chiral sorting are local findings; ligand substitution is not guaranteed to produce the same outcome in other systems.
